description: Additional validation series for S3_transport_load at mild and intermediate stress levels, anchored to CAISO Flex Alert literature. Added to strengthen range calibration in historical-analog validation package.
data_source: Extracted from existing load_sweep series (N=500/point). Same configuration as main calibrated S3 run (theta_node=0.70, stochastic_scale=0.30, theta_cascade=0.30).
validation_rationale: The main S3 calibration point (load_amount=0.40, K_cl=0.534, K_q=0.956, N=1000) demonstrates the marginal regime but is at the upper end of documented CAISO analog stress levels. CAISO Flex Alert events typically correspond to 3-8% voluntary demand reduction — a substantially milder stress. Adding load=0.15 and load=0.20 points anchors the CAISO analog more precisely in the numerical range and strengthens the range-calibration claim in validation Claim 1.

points.label: S3_caiso_mild_L015
points.literature_anchor: CAISO Flex Alert mild event (3-5% demand reduction). Grid stressed, no threshold crossing in majority of runs. Quantitative detects sub-threshold cascade propagation in 64.2% of runs vs 14.2% for classical — gap_abs=50.0pp.
points.validation_role: CAISO-like mild stress analog. Best match for documented 3-5% demand reduction events. K_cl=0.142 confirms sub-threshold stress (classical detects <15%); K_q=0.642 shows continuous propagation detectable.

points.label: S3_caiso_intermediate_L020
points.literature_anchor: CAISO Flex Alert moderate event (5-8% demand reduction). Intermediate between mild CAISO stress (load=0.15) and calibrated marginal regime (load=0.40). Maximum gap_abs=60.2pp across all S3 load points — widest method separation zone.
points.validation_role: CAISO-like intermediate stress. Shows that the quantitative-vs-classical gap PEAKS at moderate stress (not at maximum load). Useful for demonstrating sub-threshold sensitivity advantage in the most literature-relevant parameter zone.

key_findings.comparison_to_main_S3: Main point (load=0.40): K_cl=0.534, K_q=0.956, gap=0.422. Mild points (0.15/0.20) have LARGER gap_abs but lower absolute detection rates — consistent with gap peaking in sub-threshold zone.
key_findings.range_calibration_improvement: CAISO events documented as 3-8% demand reduction. Model load=0.15 (15% transport stress increase) serves as plausible upper bound for mild CAISO analog, demonstrating that K_q already detects cascade risk at this mild stress level.
